lede: Digits reach 1.210 bits per dimension and Fashion-MNIST 3.263, with broken samples from the inverse.
title: Multi-scale RealNVP
question: Does the coupling flow assign a high likelihood to grayscale MNIST, and does inverting it produce recognizable samples?
process: A coupling layer splits the channels with a mask. Where the mask is 1, the value is kept. Where it is 0, a small network reads only the kept part and predicts a scale and a shift.
The forward map applies that affine transform:
The Jacobian of a coupling is triangular, so the log-determinant is the sum of s on the changed coordinates only:
The inverse recomputes s and t from the kept part of y and undoes the affine map:

The multi-scale model stacks these layers. It squeezes 28×28 down to 14×14, applies couplings, and factors half the channels out as z1. It squeezes again to 7×7, applies couplings, and factors z2. The last block emits z3. Each piece is scored under a standard normal.
The log-density is the change-of-variables formula. Pixels are dequantized and passed through a logit first, and that Jacobian is included as well:
\[ \log p(x) = \log p(z_1)+\log p(z_2)+\log p(z_3) + \log|\det J_{\mathrm{flow}}| + \log|\det J_{\mathrm{logit}}| \]
Training minimizes the mean of −log p(x) over the batch. A sample draws the three normals, runs the inverse flow, then applies the inverse logit.

The digits checkpoint is kept apart from the Fashion-MNIST files, so the Fashion-MNIST run did not replace it. The saved digits curve stops near epoch 9, and the test line ends at the scored negative log-likelihood of 657.3 (1.210 bits per dimension; the training figures are 660.3 and 1.215). Fashion-MNIST, trained for 20 epochs with those same hyperparameters, reaches a test value of 3.263 bits per dimension. The one-epoch search that chose the hyperparameters had a validation value of 1.583 bits per dimension.

opening.summary: Epoch 20 is the Fashion-MNIST checkpoint that was scored. Its hyperparameters are the wider network from the search.

marks.summary: Epoch 20 is marked because it is the scored checkpoint. The Fashion-MNIST evaluation records a test negative log-likelihood of 1773.2 and 3.263 bits per dimension on 10,000 images. The curve is flat here. Digits, kept in their own evaluation, score a tighter test value of 1.210 bits per dimension.
marks.hover: Epoch 20, test bits per dimension 3.263, test negative log-likelihood 1773.2.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion-MNIST samples from the inverse at the epoch-20 checkpoint. A few clothes, mostly torn shapes.

marks.label: Trial 0, chosen
marks.summary: Trial 0 is marked because it has the lower validation negative log-likelihood. The saved hyperparameters are 64 hidden channels, 4 coupling layers, scale 2, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0, and batch size 128, with validation negative log-likelihood 860.1 and 1.583 bits per dimension. The objective was likelihood after one epoch, on two folds, for digits. Generation quality was not part of the score. Fashion-MNIST reused these values.
marks.hover: Negative log-likelihood 860.1. Bits per dimension 1.583. Hidden channels 64, scale 2, learning rate 0.001.
marks.frameCaption: The digit curve trained from this winning trial. The test line ends at the scored 1.21.

marks.label: Trial 1, narrower
marks.answers: How could the results be improved?
marks.summary: Trial 1 moved every free setting the other way: 32 hidden channels, scale 1, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 1e-6, and batch size 64. Validation negative log-likelihood rose to 1050.1, or 1.932 bits per dimension. The wider network and the larger step won. The saved search is these two settings, each scored after one epoch.
marks.hover: Negative log-likelihood 1050.1. Bits per dimension 1.932. Hidden channels 32, scale 1, learning rate 1e-4.
marks.frameCaption: Digit negative log-likelihood. The narrower trial was worse, and the run that was kept is the wider one.

charts.title: Inverse samples and both test scores

marks.label: Digits, inverse
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Inverting the digit flow produces a few cells that suggest a loop or a stem. Most cells are hooks, specks, and broken junctions. The VAE and f-VAE sample grids later in the report still read as digits. This grid does not.
marks.frameCaption: Digit samples from the inverse. A readable digit sits next to a broken hook.

marks.label: Fashion, inverse
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Drawing a standard normal through the inverse produces a few cells that suggest a shirt, a trouser leg, a bag, or a boot. Most are smeared gray masses. The Fashion-MNIST VAE samples keep those garment types readable.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion-MNIST samples from the inverse at the epoch-20 checkpoint. A few clothes, mostly torn shapes.

marks.label: Fashion, reconstruction
marks.valueText: Encode, then invert: clothes stay sharp
marks.summary: Eight Fashion-MNIST test images can be encoded and passed back through the inverse. The boot, the shirt, the trousers, and the plaid stay sharp. The coupling inverse preserves a real image. The soft sample grid is what the prior produces.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion-MNIST data on one row and the inverse on the next. The clothes come back.

marks.label: Digits, test set
marks.summary: The digit model was scored on its own, and the Fashion-MNIST run did not replace it. On 10,000 images the test negative log-likelihood is 657.3 and bits per dimension are 1.210. The training figures are 660.3 and 1.215. That is a much tighter density than Fashion-MNIST’s 3.263. The samples from the inverse are still stroke fragments.
marks.hover: Digit test bits per dimension 1.210. Test negative log-likelihood 657.3.
marks.frameCaption: Digit samples from the inverse of the separate checkpoint. Test bits per dimension 1.210.

reflection.worked: The digit checkpoint, kept separate from the Fashion-MNIST run, scores 1.210 test bits per dimension. Fashion-MNIST reaches 3.263 at epoch 20, and encoding an image and inverting the flow keeps real clothes. The wider Optuna trial beat the narrower one, 860.1 against 1050.1.
reflection.unexpected: Digit test bits per dimension are 1.210, and Fashion-MNIST test bits per dimension are 3.263. The digit samples from the inverse mix readable digits with broken hooks. The Fashion-MNIST samples mix a few garments with torn shapes.
reflection.why: The search is two trials of one epoch each, and Fashion-MNIST reused the digit settings. Bits per dimension can fall while the model explains the background and the prior still misses the glyph. That is a reading of the pictures, not a separate measurement. A published flow with a tight density sits nearer 1 bit, so 3.263 is only a partial fit.
reflection.improve: Keep the digit and Fashion-MNIST runs separate. Give Fashion-MNIST its own search and a longer training run. If bits per dimension keep falling while samples from the prior stay soft, add capacity in the coupling networks.
